Skills and commands

Sigma ships 46 skills. Each one is also a command you type in your agent, written /sigma-<name>. Most people only ever need the first few in the "Running work" group.

Where to start

Run /sigma-init once per repository, then /sigma-loop to work the backlog, or /sigma-goal to run a single goal with approval gates. The phase skills are called by those two; you rarely type them yourself.

Set up and healthRun once per repository, or when something looks wrong. Status and measurementRead-only views of what the loop is doing and what it cost. Running workTake goals from the backlog to merged pull requests. The phasesOne skill per step of the seven-phase flow, plus debugging. Specialist checksExtra gates for changes that carry a particular kind of risk. Shaping the backlogFrom a business idea to confirmed, scoped goals; also direction and health of the whole repository. Units of workSeveral goals sharing one branch. Team and chatCoordination between people and from a chat tool.

Set up and health

Run once per repository, or when something looks wrong.

CommandWhat it does
/sigma-initThe one setup command: scaffolds the project folder, checks access, and asks for a mode and a test command.
/sigma-setupAn alias of the init command, for people who look for it under that name.
/sigma-wizardGuides first-run setup one unresolved check at a time; it starts by itself when setup is incomplete.
/sigma-doctorChecks setup, dependencies and host support, and prints the command that fixes each problem.

Status and measurement

Read-only views of what the loop is doing and what it cost.

CommandWhat it does
/sigma-statusShows the backlog, the current iteration and the review queue.
/sigma-logReads the local action log: the active goal, its thread and recent activity.
/sigma-timeReports observed active and background time by goal, unit, skill or session.
/sigma-velocityEstimates calendar time from measured commit and pull-request throughput.
/sigma-modelPredicts the model tier a goal should run on, for phase dispatch.

Running work

Take goals from the backlog to merged pull requests.

CommandWhat it does
/sigma-loopWorks backlog goals through phase agents unattended, with verified pull requests, parking and continuing until stopped or out of budget.
/sigma-goalRuns one goal through every phase, with approval gates; the supervised route.
/sigma-chainSolves one end goal and every open prerequisite it waits on, in order, with all decisions asked up front. When to use which.
/sigma-orchestrateRuns a batch of goals as parallel sessions in dependency waves, merging and reporting. Read more.
/sigma-dagReports the stored dependency map: state, stuck and active chains, cycles. When to use which.
/sigma-triagePrioritizes and dependency-sequences a multi-goal backlog drain.
/sigma-promoteApproves AI-filed issues for the loop and repairs stuck confirmation labels.
/sigma-unparkResolves a goal that is waiting on a human and records the decision before it returns to the queue.

The phases

One skill per step of the seven-phase flow, plus debugging.

CommandWhat it does
/sigma-brainstormShapes an idea into one approved, checkable goal before any code.
/sigma-contextRecalls prior goals, graph findings and conventions as a cited brief.
/sigma-researchMaps a goal's code blast radius, existing debt and size into a short dossier.
/sigma-planWrites a bite-sized plan with files, tests and done criteria before any edit.
/sigma-plan-reviewAdversarially verifies the plan against the code and post-ship risks before implementation.
/sigma-implementImplements the plan and verifies each step.
/sigma-reviewA code-quality review: measured indicators first, then a scan across eight axes; also reviews pull requests and grades an external reviewer.
/sigma-verifyRuns the checks and shows evidence before a goal is called done.
/sigma-retroAfter shipping, assesses residual debt and proposes lessons for approval.
/sigma-debugReproduces a bug in a tight loop and diagnoses it before fixing.

Specialist checks

Extra gates for changes that carry a particular kind of risk.

CommandWhat it does
/sigma-contract-checkChecks public API, event, command-line, type or environment-variable changes for breaking consumers.
/sigma-migration-checkChecks forward migration, backfill, rollback and canary for schema or data changes.
/sigma-security-reviewThreat-models changes to authentication, user data, billing, external input or public endpoints.
/sigma-release-checkRuns the final pre-production checklist after review.

Shaping the backlog

From a business idea to confirmed, scoped goals; also direction and health of the whole repository.

CommandWhat it does
/sigma-dossierTurns a high-level business idea into a Dossier through a fixed interview, without exploring code.
/sigma-prd-intakeTurns a product requirements file into cited Dossiers plus one umbrella ticket.
/sigma-goal-designMaps a Dossier or an existing goal to code, blockers and slices in a design write-up.
/sigma-goal-reviewIndependently confirms a design write-up before its epic and slices are created.
/sigma-scopeTurns an idea into prioritized, deduplicated, dependency-linked GitHub issues.
/sigma-visionWrites a tiered product north star that grounds goals.
/sigma-alignAudits shipped goals against the north star for cumulative drift.
/sigma-auditA read-only whole-repository audit of conformance, erosion, debt and fitness.
/sigma-radarResearches current developments against the backlog and writes a ranked digest; no external writes by default.
/sigma-decideTurns an architectural decision into an enforced invariant.
/sigma-kgBuilds, refreshes or queries the optional project knowledge graph.

Units of work

Several goals sharing one branch.

CommandWhat it does
/sigma-defineOpens a new unit of work: its branch, label, registry entry and issues.
/sigma-rebaseA human-attended catch-up of a stale feature branch, with conflict resolution and verification.

Team and chat

Coordination between people and from a chat tool.

CommandWhat it does
/sigma-ledgerSets up, reads, notes and hands off through the team ledger.
/sigma-slackStarts, checks or stops the inbound Slack command listener; the Slack app itself is set up by hand.
Technical detail

Every skill is a folder with a SKILL.md whose description says when the agent should use it. On a host without slash commands (Cursor, Antigravity) the same skills are read as instructions. See Hosts for what each host runs.
